$comment: Schema version (semver, this document — NOT a blueprint field and never emitted into compiled markup). 1.0.0 = the structural IR (kinds, widths, bindings, assertions). 1.1.0 = adds the optional per-node `presentation` block (recipe/role/tone/surface/overrides) — the presentation IR.
title: Shesha blueprint IR (machine twin)
description: The JSON twin of a screen blueprint. Comprehension emits it alongside the Markdown blueprint (fenced ```blueprint-json block); form-edit's compile-blueprint.js accepts ONLY this as build input — no spec, no build (L2).

theme.description: theme token file name (e.g. 'shesha'); styling pass resolves it

property.description: camelCase entity property or dotted nav path [R-004, R-034]

component.description: explicit component type; omitted = by-datatype selection

assertions.description: placement contract verified after build (stable properties, never pixels)

node.description: A layout node — think of it as a React element. Compose the screen the way you would a React page: Stack/Row/Grid/Card for structure, Field/Text/Heading for content, Actions for buttons. The compiler maps each to the measured Shesha channel, so your flex/spacing/hierarchy instincts translate 1:1. See references/designing-like-react.md.

kind.description: layout | region: page root · stack: vertical flex · row: horizontal flex · grid: equal-width columns · card: surfaced panel · section: titled group · tabs/tab · field · text · heading · datatable · datalist · actions (Submit+exit buttonGroup) · chip. (container = alias of stack.)

title.description: card/section/tab heading, or a field's label override

width.description: flex-child width — %, px, fr or calc(); compiled to desktop.dimensions.width (the ONLY split lever [R-028])

gap.description: space between children — px number or scale token xs|sm|md|lg|xl|2xl; compiled to container gap

padding.description: inner padding — px number, scale token, or CSS shorthand; compiled to stylingBox

columns.description: kind=grid: column count (number); kind=datatable: bound column properties (string[])

property.description: kind=field: the bound entity property (camelCase / dotted path)

component.description: kind=field: explicit component type override (else by-datatype)

presentation.description: How this node LOOKS, quantized to the design system — the presentation IR. Every field is optional; a node with no `presentation` compiles exactly as before. Measured styling is never recorded as prose ("very plain"): it is quantized to the nearest recipe/role/tone/surface and, when nothing else fits, to a token path in `overrides`. The compiler resolves all of it against the ACTIVE theme (--theme), which stays the only styling input [R-042].

recipe.$comment: The enum IS the file list of shesha-form-edit/assets/blocks/*.block.json — the block library is the source of truth; add a block, add its name here.
recipe.description: a block from the block library, instantiated at this node's position (authoritative for this node — archetype chrome will not emit the same recipe twice)

role.description: what the node IS semantically: title → heading treatment · status → refListStatus chip · metric → statistic tile · meta → KeyInformationBar meta strip · body → no-op (plain content)

tone.description: the colour ROLE, never a colour: accent → brand primary/tint · neutral → surfaces + body ink · success|warning|danger → the theme's status palette. A tone the active theme does not define falls back to neutral ink.

surface.description: card → card surface (bg + hairline + radius) · band → band surface (bandBg + bottom hairline) · plain → no surface

overrides.description: escape hatch for one-off appearance: dotted path under the emitted component's `desktop` block (plus the `gap`/`padding` aliases) → a TOKEN PATH. Token paths ONLY — a raw hex or px value is a validation error, because a literal cannot follow the theme.

additionalProperties.description: a path into the active theme token file, e.g. "type.scale.titleLg", "palette.brand.tint", "spacing.4", "radius.lg", "shadow.card"
